en: Dependent on a wholesome state accompanied by initial application and sustained application, there arises a state that is neither wholesome nor accompanied by initial application and sustained application, by way of root condition.
(Abbreviated. Thirteen in the case of root; nine in the case of object ... pe ... three in the case of resultant ... pe ... thirteen in the case of non-disappearance.
(Five in the wholesome, five in the unwholesome, three in the indeterminate.)

Dependent on a wholesome state that is without applied thought but with sustained thought (*avitakkavicāramatta*), there arises a state that is neither wholesome nor without applied thought and sustained thought, by way of root condition (*hetupaccaya*).
(Abbreviated. There are thirteen [conditions] in the case of root; nine in the case of object (*ārammaṇa*) ... pe ... three in the case of result (*vipāka*) ... pe ...
thirteen in the case of non-disappearance (*avigata*).

Dependent on a wholesome state without initial application and without sustained application, there arises a state that is neither wholesome nor without initial application and sustained application by way of root condition … three.

Dependent on an indeterminate state without initial application and without sustained application, there arises a state that is neither wholesome nor without initial application and sustained application by way of root condition … three.
(Abbreviated. There are six with respect to root; six with respect to predominance … pe … three with respect to resultant … pe … six with respect to non-disappearance.
